title: ferrum.service_manifest v1
description: A versioned, reviewable description of how a service is published behind Ferrum Edge, written as TOML (ferrum-service.toml) and described here as its JSON data model. Alloy implements the producer/parser; Nexus and Foundry implement qualified read-only JSON previews. Shared v1 freeze is accepted in the canonical release candidate; publication remains pending.

x-contract.name: service-manifest

provenance.note: Alloy publishes no JSON Schema for the manifest. This schema transcribes the serde structs (deny_unknown_fields, defaults) and the checks in validate(). Cross-field rules validate() applies after defaults (for example the proxy_id default and agents.endpoint_path being below api.public_path) are not all expressible here. Re-read at the qualified 81cbb410 owner: field/bound transcription is retained; validate() also checks derived resource ID lengths after defaults, outside this schema's existing assertions. api.public_path, api.service_base_path, health.path and agents.endpoint_path share one pattern transcribing valid_path at 81cbb410: a literal absolute path with no {, }, *, ~, space, ?, #, ;, % or \, no // and no . or .. segment. Alloy main conforms again: #210 (5fe4daa) replaced valid_path with an ASCII pchar allow-list that briefly admitted ~ and *, and Alloy refuses ~ and * again since ferrum-alloy#303 (bcd0ac55af5e334f24fbef3539895842081f3968; decision in ferrum-contracts#58), so every path Alloy main accepts matches this pattern. The allow-list still refuses some characters this pattern accepts (for example ", <, [, | and non-ASCII), which keeps Alloy inside v1. This pattern is unchanged; invalid fixtures public-path-tilde.json and public-path-star.json cover ~ and *.

Alloy main's validate() (ferrum-alloy#313, unchanged on Alloy main at 0e8a96a24c149432f0c3583732d8a3875db756ce) refuses an http:// gateway.otel_endpoint unless its host is a loopback IP literal, because the export writes the endpoint into Edge's otel_tracing config without allow_plaintext and Edge drops that exporter (ferrum-contracts#82). Alloy's own fixture contracts/fixtures/manifests/orders-api.toml uses https://otel-collector:4318/v1/traces since ferrum-alloy d6e437169c15b67a8b9e218b54b4135f9a0dcc5e. Alloy and v1 share the refusal of an @ before the first / of gateway.otel_endpoint. Alloy also refuses an api.service_base_path over 2048 bytes including its trailing /, and a bare IPv4 loopback authority without a port followed directly by ? or # (for example http://127.0.0.1#frag), which Edge admits; both are stricter than this schema, so Alloy stays inside v1. Alloy's loopback check is looser than Edge's in places: it admits a few loopback spellings Edge drops (for example an expanded IPv6 loopback or a non-numeric port), which yield an exported otel_tracing config Edge omits. This schema follows Edge's canonical spelling, and ferrum-alloy#319 tracks aligning Alloy.
Edge v0.9.9 documents the MCP namespace character and length rule and requires the MCP endpoint to sit under the proxy listen path.

gateway.otel_endpoint transcribes Edge's cleartext rule from its published OtelTracingConfig schema, which src/plugins/otel_tracing.rs (validate_endpoint_for_provider, screen_cleartext_endpoint) and src/plugins/utils/socket_host.rs (is_loopback_ip_literal_endpoint) enforce: without allow_plaintext, an http:// URL is admitted only to a loopback IP literal spelled as a dotted-quad 127.d.d.d or [::1], with an optional numeric port, its authority ending at /, ? or #, or at the end of the URL after any trailing whitespace (Edge trims the configured value first). Alloy's export never writes allow_plaintext, so the manifest admits cleartext only to such a host; https:// URLs are unaffected. This is the only new constraint: whitespace, a path, ?query and #fragment are as v1 already allowed them, and v1's base pattern still refuses an @ before the first /. Two Edge runtime checks cover what this schema cannot judge, and Edge then omits the optional otel_tracing plugin. First, the url crate's parse fails for an empty host (https://:4318/...), a port that is non-numeric or out of range, a malformed IPv4 literal (an octet above 255, or a leading-zero octet that is not valid octal such as 09), or a forbidden control character in the host such as NUL. The parser first discards tab, LF and CR anywhere in the URL, so those alone do not make it fail (https://otel-<tab>collector:43<tab>18/... parses as https://otel-collector:4318/...); Edge's raw cleartext check above still reads the configured spelling. Second, after a successful parse Edge refuses a URL whose parsed username or password is non-empty; the parser skips any run of / and \ after the scheme, so https:// followed by \, / and user@collector.example/v1/traces parses with username user although v1's base pattern sees no @ before its first /. The cleartext pattern checks only the shape of the port; Edge checks its range. The schema is never stricter than Edge there. The rules are identical at v0.9.19 (510ce7121c3d9754110d330a30a3bd9b7a7b278e) and on Edge main at 812bbd1a01677525d7b664ba46ba574f546efe6b.

Upper bounds and control-character rules for the Edge fields Alloy's edge export (crates/ferrum-alloy-edge/src/export.rs) writes from the manifest (ferrum-contracts#74, ferrum-alloy#309). public_path is the proxy listen_path (500 bytes); service_base_path, without its trailing /, the proxy backend_path (2048 bytes); upstream.host the proxy backend_host, or upstream targets[].host when health is set (255 bytes); health.path the active http_path (2048 bytes); timeouts the backend_*_timeout_ms (at most 86400000); health.interval_seconds at most 3600 and health.timeout_ms at most 86400000. Edge measures string lengths in UTF-8 bytes and JSON Schema maxLength counts characters, so each maxLength is the byte limit as a character count: never stricter than Edge, exact for ASCII, and Edge itself refuses a non-ASCII value that fits the characters but not the bytes. upstream.host refuses exactly what Edge's contains_control_chars refuses (bytes below 0x20 other than tab, LF and CR). Alloy main's host rule is stricter and stays inside v1: since ferrum-alloy#313 (db412da37564ffbe869e2b40530dbebf5afe7ac8) it refuses every control and whitespace character. The four path fields (api.public_path, api.service_base_path, health.path and agents.endpoint_path) refuse every C0 control and DEL, which Alloy's valid_path already refuses (it admits only ASCII pchar bytes). The control rules are anchored lookahead patterns ([\s\S], so no line terminator ends the scan), and use only keywords the Nexus and Foundry preview compilers support. The bounds and src/config/types.rs rules are unchanged on Edge main at 6ad7cfe8c03fac254ab348691056d428bc2543a6.

public_path.description: Gateway listen path prefix, a literal absolute path. Exported as the Edge proxy listen_path, which Edge limits to 500 UTF-8 bytes (MAX_LISTEN_PATH_LENGTH). maxLength counts characters, so it equals the byte limit only for ASCII; Edge enforces the bytes. No C0 control character or DEL, as Alloy's valid_path refuses them.

service_base_path.description: Backend path prefix ending in /. Exported, without its trailing /, as the Edge proxy backend_path, which Edge limits to 2048 UTF-8 bytes (MAX_BACKEND_PATH_LENGTH): at most 2049 characters with the /. This Edge-derived boundary is the v1 bound (ferrum-contracts#82); Alloy main, Foundry and Nexus currently refuse more than 2048 characters, which is stricter and inside v1. maxLength counts characters; Edge enforces the bytes. No C0 control character or DEL, as Alloy's valid_path refuses them.

openapi.description: Path to the exported OpenAPI document, relative to the manifest.

host.description: Bare host name or address, no scheme. Exported as the Edge proxy backend_host, or upstream targets[].host when health is set, which Edge limits to 255 UTF-8 bytes (MAX_BACKEND_HOST_LENGTH). maxLength counts characters, so it equals the byte limit only for ASCII; Edge enforces the bytes of a longer non-ASCII host. Refuses exactly the control bytes Edge's contains_control_chars refuses: below 0x20 except tab, LF and CR.

path.description: Exported as the Edge upstream active health check http_path, which Edge limits to 2048 UTF-8 bytes (MAX_BACKEND_PATH_LENGTH). maxLength counts characters; Edge enforces the bytes. No C0 control character or DEL, as Alloy's valid_path refuses them.

interval_seconds.description: Exported as active.interval_seconds; Edge allows 1 to 3600 (MAX_HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL).

timeout_ms.description: Exported as active.timeout_ms; Edge allows 1 to 86400000 (MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, 24 hours).

connect_ms.description: Exported as backend_connect_timeout_ms; Edge allows at most 86400000 (MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, 24 hours).

read_ms.description: 0 disables the read timeout for long-lived streams. Exported as backend_read_timeout_ms; Edge allows at most 86400000 (MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, 24 hours).

write_ms.description: Exported as backend_write_timeout_ms; Edge allows at most 86400000 (MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, 24 hours).

otel_endpoint.description: OTLP/HTTP traces URL without credentials, written into Edge's otel_tracing config without allow_plaintext. https:// to any host, or http:// only to a loopback IP literal (127.d.d.d or [::1], optional numeric port), the only cleartext exporter Edge v0.9.19 and later keep without allow_plaintext. No @ before the first /. A path, ?query and #fragment are allowed, as Edge allows them; a consumer may refuse more. Edge trims surrounding whitespace first. It also refuses an endpoint its URL parser rejects (for example an empty host or an out-of-range port) and, after parsing, one whose parsed userinfo is non-empty (for example extra / or \ characters before user@host); this pattern does not judge either.

endpoint_path.description: Literal absolute MCP endpoint path below api.public_path. No C0 control character or DEL, as Alloy's valid_path refuses them.

namespace.description: MCP tool-name prefix; defaults to service.name.
